title: Your Income & How the IRS / ACA Counts It
blurb: How Kalshi trading results, rental income and savings interest flow into Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) — the number Medi-Cal and Covered California actually test — plus tax treatment details. Every row links to an official source; unverified items are left blank and flagged.

rows.topic: Zero earned income ≠ zero countable income
rows.finding: Medi-Cal and Covered California do not use "earned income" or pay stubs; they use MAGI (tax-based household income). Wages are only one input. Trading gains, net rental income and taxable interest all count. No job or earned income is required to qualify for either program.
rows.value: MAGI, not earned income, is the test
rows.note: Checked 2026-10-18. Marketplace (and state exchange) uses MAGI for both Marketplace savings and Medicaid eligibility.

rows.finding: MAGI = Adjusted Gross Income (Form 1040 line 11) PLUS untaxed foreign income, non-taxable Social Security benefits, and tax-exempt interest. For many people MAGI ≈ AGI.
rows.source_label: HealthCare.gov glossary — Modified Adjusted Gross Income

rows.finding: Covered California counts taxable investment income (including interest), plus income from applicable rental, wages and other categories under MAGI rules. Event-contract results require a tax classification and actual records; they are not automatically countable as a known net amount for this person.
rows.source_label: Covered California — What is financial help? ("What Counts as Income")
rows.note: Covered California lists investment income; treatment of this individual's Kalshi trades is unresolved, not established by the general list.

rows.topic: Rental income (property management of own properties)
rows.finding: Net rental income reported on Schedule E flows into AGI (Form 1040 line 8) and therefore into MAGI for Medi-Cal and Covered California purposes. Rental income is not "earned income" for Social Security purposes, but it is fully countable for coverage.
rows.value: Net Schedule E rent → AGI → MAGI
rows.source_label: IRS — Instructions for Schedule E (Form 1040) & Form 1040 instructions
rows.note: Schedule E net profit/loss is reported on Form 1040 (rental real estate, royalties, partnerships, S corps). Verified via IRS Schedule E instructions (2025 ed.).

rows.topic: Rental losses can offset other income — up to a limit
rows.finding: Rental real estate losses are passive by default and generally cannot offset non-rental income. Exception: with "active participation" (e.g., you make management decisions such as approving tenants, rental terms, repair expenditures), up to $25,000 of loss can offset nonpassive income if MAGI ≤ $100,000; phased down 50% of the excess until fully phased out at MAGI $150,000. A separate "real estate professional" exception exists (Publication 925). This can legitimately lower AGI — and therefore MAGI for coverage.
rows.note: Verified against Pub 527 and 2025 Instructions for Form 8582 (irs.gov). Real-estate-professional test is complex — see flagged item FL-05.

rows.finding: Interest on bank/savings accounts is taxable interest income (reported via Schedule B / Form 1099-INT) and is included in AGI and MAGI. Healthcare.gov instructs applicants to include all interest and dividends, "including tax-exempt interest," when estimating Marketplace income.

rows.topic: Kalshi contract profit and tax forms
rows.finding: Taxable income generally must be reported even without a Form 1099, but the precise tax characterization, netting and which forms are issued for this person's Kalshi contracts cannot be certified from the government materials cited here. The company's help page is contextual, not an IRS ruling.
rows.source_label: IRS — Publication 550 (general investment income and reporting)
rows.note: Company documentation, not official tax authority: https://help.kalshi.com/en/articles/13823849-what-tax-documentation-does-kalshi-provide . Flag FL-01.

rows.topic: Section 1256 (60/40) treatment of Kalshi event contracts
rows.finding: General §1256 rules do not establish that this taxpayer's Kalshi event contracts qualify for 60/40 treatment or a particular tax form. CFTC exchange designation is a regulatory fact, not an IRS contract-by-contract tax ruling.
rows.source_label: IRS — Publication 550 (§1256 contracts and general investment rules)
rows.note: CFTC designation: https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8302-20 . No specific Kalshi tax characterization inferred. Flag FL-01.

rows.finding: KalshiEX LLC received a CFTC Order of Designation as a Designated Contract Market (DCM) on Nov 3-4, 2020; its affiliate Kalshi Klear LLC received a DCO Order of Registration Aug 29, 2024. DCM status supports the exchange's legitimacy but does NOT itself determine tax classification.

rows.topic: Whether Kalshi trading is self-employment income for this taxpayer
rows.finding: IRS Schedule SE instructions describe general exclusions for certain investment proceeds; application depends on the taxpayer's actual business and contract classification. Neither non-dealer status nor an exemption from self-employment tax has been established for this person.
rows.note: General rules cannot be applied to this taxpayer's Kalshi activity without facts and a supported tax classification. Flag FL-01.

rows.topic: Capital losses can lower AGI (and thus MAGI)
rows.finding: Net capital losses offset capital gains with no limit; any excess loss can offset up to $3,000 of other income per year ($1,500 MFS), with unlimited carryover to future years. For a trading year with net losses, AGI (hence MAGI) can be pushed toward zero or reduced by the $3,000 — directly relevant to Medi-Cal eligibility.
rows.source_label: IRS — Tax Topic 409, Capital gains and losses
rows.note: Checked 2026-10-18. Reporting: Form 8949/Schedule D, or Form 6781 for §1256 contracts.

rows.topic: 0% federal capital-gains rate for low taxable income
rows.finding: For tax years beginning in 2025, net long-term capital gain is taxed at 0% if taxable income is at/below $48,350 (single). At low MAGI you may owe $0 federal tax on gains even while those gains still COUNT for Medi-Cal/Marketplace income tests (tax ≠ income for eligibility).
rows.effective: TY2025 published; TY2026 thresholds not in this source
rows.note: 2026 threshold amounts: not published on the source consulted — left blank, see flag FL-06.

rows.finding: A 3.8% NIIT applies to net investment income (including trading gains, rents from non-professional activities, and interest) for individuals with MAGI over $200,000 ($250,000 MFJ). Irrelevant to eligibility planning but material to after-tax cash.
rows.source_label: IRS — Tax Topic 559, Net investment income tax (linked from Topic 409)

rows.topic: Federal tax filing threshold 2026 (context for CA mandate exemption)
rows.finding: For tax year 2026 the basic standard deduction is $16,100 single / $32,200 married filing jointly (raised from $15,000/$30,000 by the OBBBA, which set $15,750/$31,500 for TY2025). A single filer generally must file a federal return only if gross income meets/exceeds the standard deduction. Under California's individual mandate, income BELOW the federal filing threshold is an automatic exemption.
rows.note: Cross-reference: FTB health care mandate page (income below filing threshold = exempt).

rows.topic: Estimated tax payments on volatile gains
rows.finding: If you have taxable capital gains you may owe quarterly estimated tax (Form 1040-ES) — no employer withholding occurs on trading/rental income. Underpayment interest can accrue; safe-harbor rules are in Pub 505.

rows.topic: HSA as an above-the-line MAGI lever (new for 2026 in California)
rows.finding: IRS Publication 969 describes HSA eligibility, contribution limits and deductions for eligible individuals. Earning wages is not itself a condition for contributing; qualifying health coverage, Medicare, other coverage and dependent status matter. HSA eligibility and deductions for this person are not established by the mere availability of a Bronze plan.
rows.note: Plan-specific 2026 changes: https://www.coveredca.com/important-changes . Do not assume a tax or MAGI reduction without personal eligibility.

rows.topic: Unverified personal annual and monthly MAGI for coverage
rows.finding: No numerical scenario can be assigned without the individual's actual taxable rental amounts, interest, household and tax characterization of Kalshi contracts. The $22,025 one-person Medi-Cal reference is for 2026 only; $31,920 is a 2027 marketplace state-aid reference, not a guaranteed individual outcome.
rows.note: Marketplace 2027: https://www.coveredca.com/pdfs/FPL-chart.pdf . A tax or county determination is required.
